name: Nyan Parlor
tagline: An AI fortune-telling parlor that runs tarot pulls, I Ching casts and BaZi charts, then keeps talking to you in character.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Every mechanical part of this is public domain math and public domain text. A 78 card tarot deck with reversals is a shuffle, an I Ching cast is six coin flips mapped to a hexagram table, and BaZi is a calendar conversion that open source Chinese lunar libraries already do correctly. The only real work is the persona and the prompt that turns a draw into a reading that feels like it was written for you, and an agent can produce a decent version of that on the first pass. What you cannot one-shot is the taste: the pacing, the cat, the art, the restraint not to sound like a horoscope generator. So you get the engine easily and the charm roughly.
coreLoopDIY: Draws a spread or casts a hexagram or computes a BaZi chart locally, feeds the deterministic result plus your question to an LLM with a fixed persona prompt, then keeps the conversation going with the draw pinned in context.
requirements: Node 20 and a local SQLite file
An LLM API key (Anthropic or OpenAI) in .env.local
An open source Chinese lunar calendar library for BaZi pillars
Optional: public domain Rider Waite card scans if you want pictures
whatYouLose: The character writing, which is most of why these apps are fun and the hardest part to fake
Card and UI art that someone actually art directed instead of a grid of placeholder rectangles
Mobile polish and a session history that survives you closing the laptop, unless you build it
A free tier: every reading now costs you tokens
Any confidence that the BaZi engine handles true solar time and solar term edge cases the way a specialist would
moatNotes: The divination systems are centuries old and uncopyrightable. The moat is entirely tone, art and the feeling that the thing on the other side has a personality.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because nobody opens a fortune-telling app for the hexagram lookup table. They open it to be told something in a voice they like, at a moment when they want to hear it, and a polished persona with decent art does that in a way your localhost chat window does not. Freemium also means the first reading costs nothing, which beats wiring up an API key and paying per token for a novelty you might use four times a year.
notes: The randomness is trivial, the mysticism is free, the cat is the product.
prompt:
Build a local AI divination parlor as a single Next.js 15 app using the App Router, TypeScript and Tailwind. No accounts, no cloud sync, no analytics, no telemetry.

Stack, do not substitute: Next.js 15, SQLite through better-sqlite3, Anthropic Messages API read from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.local. Create .env.example and never commit real keys. Start with npm run dev, nothing else.

Three deterministic engines, pure TypeScript, each with unit tests and zero network calls:
1. Tarot: full 78 card deck as typed data with upright and reversed meaning strings. Support three spreads: single card, past/present/future, and Celtic Cross. Use crypto.getRandomValues for the shuffle, not Math.random.
2. I Ching: six simulated three coin casts, build the hexagram bottom up, track changing lines, resolve to one of 64 hexagrams with name, judgement and image text, plus the transformed hexagram when lines change.
3. BaZi: take birth date, time and timezone, use the lunar-typescript package to compute the four pillars with heavenly stems and earthly branches, plus the day master and the five element counts. Do not hand roll the calendar conversion.

UI: one page, chat transcript on the right, a left panel to pick the method and enter inputs. The user asks a question, the engine runs locally, the raw structured result is rendered as a small card in the transcript, then streamed interpretation appears below it. After the first reading the user can keep chatting and the model must keep the original draw in context and must not silently redraw.

Persona: define it in one editable file at lib/persona.ts. Default voice is a calm, slightly sardonic parlor host who reads the cards as given and never promises outcomes. Add a one line disclaimer in the footer that this is entertainment.

Persist every session in SQLite: question, method, raw engine output as JSON, full message history. Add a sidebar list of past sessions and a plain JSON export button.

Out of scope: payments, user accounts, image generation, card artwork beyond simple CSS cards, native mobile, push notifications, multi-language support beyond English.

Finish with a README covering setup, where to edit the persona, and how to add a new divination engine behind the shared engine interface.
